title: U.S. House · New York's 13th District
area: Upper Manhattan, including Harlem, Washington Heights, and Inwood, plus part of the west Bronx.

context.text: Incumbent Adriano Espaillat lost the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary to Darializa Avila Chevalier, 45.7% to 49.5% (Avila Chevalier also defeated Oscar Romero and Theo Chino-Tavarez). Espaillat is not on the November ballot.

Two other candidates who had qualified for general-election ballot lines, Bob Cohen (Working Families Party) and Candace Niles (Voice Party), withdrew or were disqualified before the general election, leaving a two-way race.

candidates.name: Darializa Avila Chevalier
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, defeating incumbent Adriano Espaillat
candidates.currentRole: None (public defender's office investigator; doctoral student)

priorities.text: "Darializa will fight to abolish the deportation machine, expand pathways to citizenship, secure free legal representation for immigrants, and more."
"Darializa will fight to divest the billions of taxpayer dollars we spend on senseless wars abroad, and invest those funds in child tax credits, baby bonds, and more."
"Darializa will fight to protect all tenants, fully fund Section 8, fully fund NYCHA, prevent deed theft, and build affordable housing."

"Darializa will fight for Medicare for All: a free, universal system that covers primary and mental health care, dental, vision, hearing, reproductive care, long-term care, and lower prescription costs."
"Darializa will never take money from corporate PACs, and will fight against monopolies, price gouging, and super PACs."

positions.summary: Campaigns on abolishing ICE and expanding pathways to citizenship rather than expanding immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: Darializa will fight to abolish the deportation machine, expand pathways to citizenship, secure free legal representation for immigrants, and more.

positions.summary: Campaigns on protecting tenants, fully funding Section 8 and NYCHA, and preventing deed theft.
positions.quote: Darializa will fight to protect all tenants, fully fund Section 8, fully fund NYCHA, prevent deed theft, and build affordable housing.

positions.summary: Supports a Medicare for All system covering primary, mental health, dental, vision, hearing, reproductive, and long-term care.
positions.quote: Darializa will fight for Medicare for All: a free, universal system that covers primary and mental health care, dental, vision, hearing, reproductive care, long-term care, and lower prescription costs.

positions.summary: Lists raising the minimum wage among her economic-security priorities.
Says she will not take corporate PAC money and campaigns against corporate greed and monopolies, and on redirecting spending from military budgets to domestic programs.
positions.quote: Darializa will never take money from corporate PACs, and will fight against monopolies, price gouging, and super PACs.

positions.summary: Campaigns for investing funds redirected from military spending into child tax credits and baby bonds.
positions.quote: Darializa will fight to divest the billions of taxpayer dollars we spend on senseless wars abroad, and invest those funds in child tax credits, baby bonds, and more.

candidates.name: Manual Williams
candidates.currentRole: None (U.S. Army veteran and reservist; paralegal and small-business owner)

priorities.text: Campaigns against New York City's sanctuary city policy, saying it should end.
Supports the SAVE Act and photo voter ID requirements, and has litigated against the New York City Board of Elections over what he calls election-system loopholes.
Opposes reducing police funding and calls for fully funding public safety alongside changes to the criminal justice system.
Describes an economic approach he calls "Universal Capitalism," focused on expanding working families' access to capital and wealth-building.

positions.summary: Opposes cutting police funding and calls for fully funding public safety while overhauling the criminal justice system.
positions.quote: No to Defund Police • Fully fund public safety • Execute complete Criminal Justice System (CJS) Overhaul

positions.summary: Campaign website says he supports the SAVE Act and voter ID and describes litigation against the Board of Elections over election-system loopholes.
positions.quote: YES to SAVE Act & Voter ID

positions.summary: Campaign website lists protecting women's sports and private spaces among its priorities, alongside a two-gender standard.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign-finance activity was reported to the FEC as of Ballotpedia's most recent data. Positions above are drawn from his own campaign website, which frames most of its content as direct comparisons to and criticism of his opponent; those comparative and characterizing claims about her positions and personal history are not included here because they are not independently verifiable and the site itself flags some as "alleged." Only Williams's own stated positions, in his own words, are reflected.

researchNotes: Federal incumbents' key floor votes and FEC campaign-finance totals are added separately by script. This race has no incumbent on the November ballot, since Adriano Espaillat lost his primary. Manual Williams's campaign website consists largely of point-by-point attacks on his opponent; only his own affirmative positions, stated in his own words, are reflected in this file.
